subject: Approval request: 3-year fixed pricing with renewal protection — Orion Data Labs
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 1 May 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Approval request: 3-year fixed pricing + renewal protection for Orion Data Labs

Team —

Following a productive week with Orion Data Labs (Dana Liu, Kyle Smith), they have signaled willingness to commit to a 3-year enterprise agreement with material committed spend, subject to three non-standard asks that require executive/deal-desk approval:

- Price lock: hold current list-derived unit rates for 36 months (no upward repricing during term).
- Uplift cap: allow annual uplift capped at 5% (explicit cap to preserve predictability).
- Renewal protection: include a clause that gives Orion the option to renew at the lower of (a) current contracted rate or (b) then-applicable list minus a 10% floor to avoid sharp step-ups at renewal.

Commercial terms in brief: 35% effective discount in year 1, tiered usage commitments (minimum $1.2M ARR year 1 escalating to $2.5M by year 3), 20% of total committed value to be prepaid or secured by PO. If we accept the price-lock + uplift cap + renewal protection the deal becomes highly likely to close in Q2.

Attachments: Orion_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW), pricing_model.xlsx (scenario P&L), redwood-term-sheet.docx (proposed clauses).

Requesting: executive confirmation to approve the non-standard long-term price lock and renewal protection, or guidance on modified uplift cap (finance prefers lower cap). Legal will need to review language but we want to lock commercial direction by EOD Fri, May 4 to align with their procurement window.

Quick asks:
- Markus: your sign-off on principle (yes/no) and any guardrails you want.
- Laura: finance view on unit economics and runway impact.
- Priyom / Marissa: recommended final language/thresholds you want in the clause.

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 May 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: 3-year fixed pricing + renewal protection for Orion Data Labs

Thanks Mina — quick thoughts:

- Strategic: Orion is a valuable reference target in the data analytics vertical; long-term commitment is aligned with our go-to-market priorities.
- Risk: full 3-year price lock + 5% uplift cap is aggressive. I'd prefer tightening the uplift cap to 4% and include an annual usage floor that converts any shortfall to a variable true-up rather than carry forward.
- Controls: Legal needs to review the renewal protection wording carefully to avoid an evergreen that blocks us from re-pricing for new product tiers.

Please ask Finance for the modeled downside (3-year present value at 3% discount) and have Legal draft a short clause that preserves the ability to add materially new products at market rates.

-Markus

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: 3-year fixed pricing + renewal protection for Orion Data Labs

Mina / team —

Reviewed the attached pricing_model.xlsx and ran a downside scenario with the 5% uplift cap and the proposed renewal protection (10% floor at renewal). High-level:

- Base-case IRR still positive given their committed escalator in consumption, but the downside (usage plateauing at year 2 levels) could reduce three-year gross margin by ~6 percentage points versus our standard multi-year contract.
- A 5% uplift cap materially limits our ability to manage inflation and incremental product cost over 3 years. 4.5% reduces downside exposure meaningfully; 4% is safer but may hurt close probability.
- Conditional approval: Finance is comfortable provided we include a minimum annual consumption floor (e.g., 80% of committed run-rate) that triggers a true-up and prevents an effective permanent discount. Also recommend the renewal protection be limited to a single renewal term (one renewal option) and include language that excludes materially new product modules introduced after contract execution.

If the team accepts 4.5% cap + 80% floor + single renewal option, Finance will sign off and we can forecast the impact for forecast refresh. See attached "pricing_model.xlsx" (tab: downside_scenarios).

-Laura

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: 3-year fixed pricing + renewal protection for Orion Data Labs

Folks —

Consolidating feedback and proposing a single, executable set of commercial terms we can present to Orion this week:

1) 36-month price lock on agreed SKUs (no repricing within term).
2) Annual uplift cap: 4.5% (meets halfway between Markus & Finance).
3) Renewal protection: Orion has one option to renew for a single 12-month term at the lower of (i) contracted rates or (ii) then-current list minus 10%, subject to both: (a) minimum 80% consumption of committed run-rate during the prior term and (b) exclusion for materially new product modules.
4) Shortfall protection: if annual consumption < 80% of committed run-rate, we apply a pro-rata true-up to make Redwood whole for the contracted minimum.
5) Prepay incentive: 2% additional discount for 20% prepayment.

This preserves commercial value while addressing Orion's procurement concerns. Legal to review language; if Legal signs off we should send for procurement and request a PO by May 12. I attach a redlined term sheet (redwood-term-sheet.docx).

Priyom
Deal Desk Manager

Approved.

I authorize the Deal Desk (Priyom) to proceed with the consolidated terms: 36-month price lock on agreed SKUs, 4.5% annual uplift cap, single renewal option with 10% floor, 80% consumption floor and pro-rata true-up, and exclusion of materially new modules. Legal to finalize redline and route to DocuSign. Finance already concurred conditionally; thanks Laura.

Please move to execution and keep me posted on PO timing.

-Markus
